app_info.subtitle: Clickable decisions in chat
app_info.description: Decision Picker turns explicit choices into inline single-choice or bounded multi-select controls, then returns the user's final selection to the conversation in both readable and structured form.

justifications.read_only_justification: Validates and renders decision data without creating, updating, or deleting external records.
justifications.open_world_justification: Does not publish content or modify any public or third-party system.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not delete, overwrite, revoke, transact, or perform irreversible external actions.

test_cases.description: Render a card-based single choice with a recommended option.
test_cases.user_prompt: Ask me to choose between Fixed positions and Deterministic Random using clickable cards. Mark Deterministic Random as recommended, but do not preselect it.
test_cases.expected_output: Renders two clickable cards, visually marks only Deterministic Random as recommended, and submits the clicked option immediately.

test_cases.description: Render a list-based single choice with descriptive alternatives.
test_cases.user_prompt: Show a clickable list asking whether we should prioritize Speed, Quality, or Cost. Give each choice a short explanation and let me pick exactly one.
test_cases.expected_output: Renders three descriptive list choices and returns the selected option to the conversation after one click.

test_cases.description: Use single choice for a binary approve or reject decision.
test_cases.user_prompt: Give me two clickable options: Approve this proposal or Reject this proposal. Explain each option briefly and treat it as a normal single choice.
test_cases.expected_output: Renders a two-option single-choice decision and returns whichever option the user clicks without introducing a separate approve/reject interaction type.

test_cases.description: Render a bounded multi-select decision with an explicit submit action.
test_cases.user_prompt: Let me select exactly two priorities from Reliability, Accessibility, Performance, and Documentation. Use clickable choices with descriptions and a Submit button.
test_cases.expected_output: Renders a multi-select control that accepts exactly two selections, keeps Submit disabled until the selection is valid, and submits only through the explicit Submit action.

test_cases.description: Render a compact segmented single choice and allow server-generated decision identity.
test_cases.user_prompt: Ask me whether the rollout should be Slow, Normal, or Fast using a segmented clickable control. I only need to choose one.
test_cases.expected_output: Renders a segmented single-choice control, generates a stable decision identifier when one was not supplied, and returns the clicked selection.

negative_test_cases.description: Do not trigger for analysis that does not ask the user to make a choice.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Compare PostgreSQL and MySQL for a small SaaS backend and explain the tradeoffs.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: The app should not be invoked because the user requested analysis rather than an interactive decision.

negative_test_cases.description: Do not trigger to execute an external action.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Deploy my application to production and restart the service.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: The app should not be invoked because it presents choices but does not deploy, restart, or mutate external systems.

negative_test_cases.description: Do not trigger for unsupported free-form text input.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Ask me to write a paragraph describing what I thought about the workshop.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: The app should not be invoked because v1 supports explicit choices only, not free-form text entry.
